text:
Marathon Petroleum rose modestly today after falling sharply over the prior two trading days, as oil markets stabilized on news of potential talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz—a critical chokepoint for global crude shipments. US oil prices held steady around $96 per barrel, and refineries continued running at 94% capacity, which supports stable margins for refiners like Marathon even as crude prices remain elevated by historical standards.

The broader picture remains turbulent: diesel prices have spiked to $6.51 per gallon nationally, and there's active political debate over a potential export ban that could disrupt refinery economics. While the geopolitical uncertainty around Iran and the Middle East has been weighing on the stock (down 0.56% over two weeks despite today's bounce), any concrete shift toward reopening shipping lanes could ease supply concerns and support refiner profitability going forward.
